summary: Computed Rips persistence (H0, H1; ripser) of the (★)-certificate clouds (log u, log B, log C)/log p for 2418 primes p ≡ 1 (4) in [10⁶, 1.2·10⁶], comparing the 100 lowest-R primes (R = 4–8) with the 100 highest (R = 72–82). After regressing each feature on log #points, hard and easy groups do not differ: permutation p = 0.42 (H0 total), 0.27 (H1 total), 0.23 (H1 count) (EVIDENCE). Hard primes have 2–4 unordered certificates, so their 'topology' is just their count; persistence adds no descriptor beyond R(p).

Read BRAINSTORM/prob_lottery_model.md §§3.2–3.4 (compound-Poisson bulk, κ ≈ 3.06, calibrated to the 10⁻⁵ quantile, predicted P(f_II = 0) ≈ exp(−λ/κ)) and DISPROOF_AVENUES.md §4 (zero law −log P(0) ∝ μ^β, β ≈ 0.91, fitted on a ladder of sibling lotteries m/n where zeros are actually observable, then extrapolated with the heavy-tail family in §4.5). A tilted Kubilius sampler would only estimate the tail of a model whose tail is already analytic (Poisson/compound-Poisson). Real-world 'splitting' (conditioning p to kill slices) is DISPROOF_AVENUES §5's adversarial D1–D4 designs at 10¹⁸–10²⁵. The item adds no new test of the real tail.

The repo-status 'untried' is wrong: DISPROOF_AVENUES.md §4.1–4.3 (scripts/z32_ladder.c) already computes Type II failure sets of m/p for m = 4…24, all primes ≤ 10⁸. Failures thin out with m (m = 6: 13, last 2521; m = 8: 21; m = 12: 169; m = 24: still failing at 10⁸). A universal zero law in the cell mean μ, P(f = 0) ≈ exp(−0.535 μ^0.91), is fitted across all m, plus a one-constant crossover law predicting p_last. This is exactly the requested 'expected count vs failure rate across the numerator' threshold picture, at 100× the proposed range.

Classified the repeated-denominator slices exactly (PROVED, two lines). x = y = z is impossible. For 4/p = 2/x + 1/z with p prime, p divides x or z. If z = pk, then (4k−1) | p. If x = pk, then (2k−1) | p and z = (p+1)/4. Both are impossible for p ≡ 1 (mod 4). So every solution at every prime p ≡ 1 (4) has three distinct denominators, while every p ≡ 3 (4) has a repeated one (brute check, primes < 3000: all 218 p ≡ 3 (4) yes, all p ≡ 1 (4) no). The repeated-term slice is empty exactly where ES is hard, so there is nothing to deform.

Literature: Feng (hal-03216035, 2021) proves a DDT arcsine law for divisors in residue classes, but only as a Cesàro mean over n at a fixed modulus. No version exists for the ES coupling (modulus 4C tied to N = 4Cp+1) at a fixed n. Numerics, 300 primes near 10⁶ (9540 certificates): log d/log N for the certificate divisors is a tent peaked at 1/2 (0.23 per decile at 0.4–0.6, 0.016 at the ends), not arcsine. All divisors of the same N do follow the arcsine law (0.147 at the ends). This is forced, not informative: d ≡ d′ ≡ −1 (mod 4C) puts both d and N/d in [4C−1, N/(4C−1)], and mixing over log-harmonic C gives the tent. log C/log p decreases linearly (0.26 in the first decile, 0 in the last), i.e. the known harmonic-in-C mass. The arcsine law only says how the mass inside each window is shaped; it does not point to a better C-range.

4xyz = n(xy+yz+zx) is linear in each variable: z(4xy − n(x+y)) = nxy. So no Vieta 'flip in one variable' exists. The repo already proves this: BRAINSTORM/cayley_markoff_cm.md P3 shows no involutions, BRAINSTORM/apollonian_reciprocity.md (Q1/Q2) notes the same plus BL Lemma 3.10 (finitely many integral points off the lines at fixed n), and BRAINSTORM/bsA_fricke_vieta.md F2 shows the genuine Markoff/Fricke cubic attached to ES words has Vieta moves only on the fibre, never changing the ES data. U_n is birational to a plane in reciprocal coordinates, so its birational group is Cremona-sized but carries no integral structure. A QRT-type invariant would need a non-trivial integral-preserving map, and none exists beyond S₃.

Both one-series relaxations of 'p/4 Ω from three integer resistors' were worked out by hand, and both are trivial (PROVED). Parallel{x, y, (c+d) in series} is literally ES with z = c+d. Series{k, parallel(x, y)} asks for 4/(p−4k) = 1/x + 1/y, which for odd m = p−4k holds iff m has a prime factor ≡ 3 (mod 4). Taking p − 4k ≡ 0 (mod 3) (k ≡ p (mod 3), 0 < k < p/4) always works, so every p/4 is realisable with one series link. The resistor language adds no constraint between 'trivial' and 'exactly ES', and the series-parallel (Stern–Brocot) combinatorics concern resistances from unit resistors, not three-term unit-fraction sums.

Thin lenses in contact have ray-transfer matrices [[1,0],[−1/f,1]], which lie in an abelian unipotent group. Their product [[1,0],[−(1/x+1/y+1/z),1]] just restates the sum, with no SL₂(ℤ) word structure. Lenses separated by gaps d give words in [[1,d],[0,1]] and [[1,0],[−P,1]], which are SL₂(ℤ) continued-fraction words only when the powers P = 1/f are integers. ES's integer focal lengths give non-integral powers, so the optics model does not match the repo's SL₂ form ([[a,p],[c,d]], c ∈ 4ℕ, FRONTIER §2.1) or the M(a) = TᵃS words (bsA_fricke_vieta). The dictionary is either trivial (contact) or lands outside SL₂(ℤ) (gaps).

BRAINSTORM/bsA_selling_sandpile.md D2–D3 already gives the sandpile reading (critical group ℤ/n, genus = sandpile pairing). This item's new angle is whether S_e = {ab⁻¹ mod e : ab | N}, N = (p+e)/4, is a subgroup or coset. Computed for all p ≡ 1 (4) < 10⁴ and e ≡ 3 (4), e < 64 (9739 slices). S_e is closed under multiplication in 35% of slices, mostly because it fills a small (ℤ/e)^×; it is a proper nontrivial subgroup in only 10%, typically |S_e| ≤ 11. Of the 6188 slices missing −1, 41% miss it because the group H generated by N's primes misses −1, and 59% have −1 ∈ H but the bounded-exponent subset products miss it (EVIDENCE). So S_e is a box, not a group, and no group-theoretic shortcut for '−1 ∈ S_e' exists beyond the H-level (character/genus) condition the repo already uses.

The 'critical exponent' asked for, i.e. the decay of the surviving (uncovered) class density as the identity/witness modulus grows, is the repo's profinite avoider density δ*(T). DISCOVERIES.md (H)7 (POINTWISE_SIZE) estimates it by Monte Carlo with multilevel splitting: −log δ*(T) ≍ (log T)^{2.3…2.6} (EVIDENCE). (H)10 / POINTWISE_OMEGA Thm 9.3 proves log(1/δ*(T)) ≤ T^{1/3+o(1)} (PROVED), and the mod-840/9240/120120 uncovered classes for m = 4…12 are tabulated in MODEL_SPECIFIC §4.1. The smooth-modulus survival curve over primes is BRAINSTORM/tech_smooth_level.md §4. Nothing in the item goes beyond these.

Wrote down the proposed per-C CSP: variables ε_q for q | N = 4Cp+1 (exponent choices for prime powers), one constraint Π q^{ε_q} ≡ −1 (mod 4C). Its factor graph is a star (one global group constraint), so BP/cavity is exact and equals the finite Fourier expansion #sol = φ(4C)⁻¹ Σ_χ χ(−1) Π_{q^k∥N} (Σ_{j≤k} χ(q)^j). Different C share no variables (different integers N), so there is no loopy interaction and no replica structure. The 'cavity estimate' is therefore exactly the repo's character split R = M_gen + X (FRONTIER §2.1) and its first-moment main term τ(N)/φ(4C) (BM_CORRECTED_COUNT); the 'hard structure' is the known genus/BM layer. The binary-carry encoding alt step (#SAT on bits) is a different, much looser model with no statistical-physics leverage.

Computed C_min(p) (least C with a divisor d ≡ −1 (mod 4C) of 4Cp+1, the (★) line, cap 10⁵) for all 2 880 504 primes p ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 10⁸ in 9 s. It fails exactly at the census's 14 (★)-sterile primes (last 8 813 281), a cross-check. The record is C_min = 41 027 at p = 85 664 329. The tail is a power law, P(C_min > x) ≈ x^{−α}, whose exponent grows with p: the slope over x ∈ [8, 64] is α = 1.22 / 1.65 / 1.90 on [10⁵, 10⁶] / [10⁶, 10⁷] / [10⁷, 10⁸], and P(C_min > 32) = 1.9e-3 / 8.1e-4 / 3.8e-4 (EVIDENCE). That is exactly the lottery model, per-level hit mass ≈ log p/φ(4C) ⇒ P(C_min > x) ≈ x^{−κ log p} (ratio of α 1.56 vs predicted 1.33, noisy). So the tail is neither p-independent scale-free nor exponential; nothing beyond the repo's a_min / least-family-size calibrations (DISCOVERIES (H)5, z52b_dividing #311).

BRAINSTORM/s3_lll_lenstra.md already does this item. It places Type II certificates on Lenstra-regime lines (58% for primes < 3000), Coppersmith-only (28%) and below N^{1/4} (14%), with at most 1 pair per Lenstra line. It records that Lenstra/CHGN give only upper bounds and decision procedures, and that a Minkowski short vector does not supply the root. BRAINSTORM/z52_lit_divisor_class.md verifies Lenstra 1984 (Thm p. 332), CHGN 2008, Hales arXiv:2410.05030 and Bernstein 2008 Thm 6.4 from primary sources, all with the 'no existence forcing' relation. The item's extra hope, a determinant structure explaining the log²p count, fails for the same reason: the lattice certifies at most O(1) hits per line, never ≥ 1.

The proposed Z3 instance ('p ≡ 1 mod 840 and (4uC−1) ∤ p+u for all u, C ≤ K') is a pure single-class CRT avoidance system. It is never UNSAT, because p ≡ 1 mod lcm(all moduli) satisfies it (4uC−1 > u+1) — the square-class witness, i.e. Mordell–Schinzel again. So SAT gives only CRT points, and a sieve finds them directly. Least avoiding primes: K = 20: 52081 (R = 4), 89041, 97441. K = 40: 206641 (R = 2), 680401, and 712321, one of the census's 14 (★)-sterile primes (R = 0; ES still holds there via other lines) (CERTIFIED by the sieve). Building p to dodge small certificates is the repo's 'class of one' adversarial design (DISPROOF_AVENUES §5, D1–D4 at 10¹⁸–10²⁵), so a SAT solver adds nothing beyond CRT.

Π₁ status is already PROVED in BRAINSTORM/z45_transfer_logic.md: sorted bounds x ≤ n, y ≤ 2n², z ≤ 2n⁴ make ES(n) a bounded formula, provable in PA. So no n² bound is needed for the logical classification, and z45 also covers the model-theoretic consequences. Small new check: every (★) solution has max(x,y,z) = n·max(u,B)·C ≤ n(n+u+B)/4 ≤ n²/2 (PROVED, using u+B ≤ n). The 14 (★)-sterile primes ≤ 10¹⁰ all have general Type II solutions (c ≥ 2) with max ≤ 0.503 n², worst p = 577 (EVIDENCE/CERTIFIED by exact check). So 'a solution with max ≤ n²' holds for primes up to the (★) census range. A web search for ES + bounded arithmetic found nothing; whether IΔ₀+exp proves ES is not answerable cheaply and carries no proof-shape constraint beyond z45's.

I did not train a transformer. Instead I ran the cheaper diagnostic (alt step tools-0222): a residue-only baseline on whether 4p+1 has a prime factor ≡ 3 (4), i.e. whether (★) has a C = 1 certificate. Logistic regression on one-hot p mod q for q ≤ 97, trained on p < 4·10⁶ and tested out of range on p ∈ [2·10⁷, 2.2·10⁷], reaches AUC 0.955 and accuracy 0.922 against a 0.786 majority rate (EVIDENCE). That signal is exactly the exact rule 'some q ≡ 3 (4), q ≤ 97, has p ≡ −1/4 (mod q)'; the remainder depends on large prime factors. So the learnable part is small-prime divisibility, which is what Charton's GCD models learn (base/small-prime divisibility rules). Anything a sequence model could add would be a factoring shortcut, and an extrapolating search algorithm would not be a proof of existence anyway.

TFNP placement is in BRAINSTORM/logic_complexity.md and BRAINSTORM/z31_complexity.md (a)(2)/(b). These give ES-SEARCH ∈ TFNP if ES holds, the witnessing theorems (S¹₂ → FP, T¹₂ → PLS), Jeřábek's FACTOR ∈ PPA ∩ PPP (randomised), and the hardness transfer that an ES-five solver outputs a QNR, so a poly-time solver would derandomise QNR-finding (CONSTRUCTIVE_ES (J)35). The PPA (parity) template is WINDMILL.md §1 (PROVED reduction: any windmill gives an explicit weight with Σw odd for every p) plus §§2–3 and WINDMILL_REDUCTION §6. Those prove that integral-affine windmills don't exist, and an exhaustive GF(2) feature search found no generalising odd-weight law. The item's PPA template is exactly that reduction. PPP/PLS placements would need a proof of ES, as the item says.

B2_ACROSS_FIELDS §M5 already notes that a count congruence must see primality, because the Type I/II count is 0 at odd squares. WINDMILL.md §§0–3 found f, f_I, f_II parities random to 6·10⁴ (f(97) = 8 is even). New check on the (★) count (R(p) is even, PROVED): R(p)/2 mod 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 over all 12 980 primes p ≡ 1 (4) < 3·10⁵ is uniform (mod 2: 6503/6477; mod 3: 4424/4275/4281, +1.8σ at 0) (EVIDENCE). No class mod 24 or mod 840 (≥ 20 primes) has a constant residue of R/2 mod 2, 3 or 4. No Chen-type orbit-size divisibility is visible, and Chevalley–Warning has no foothold: the ES variety mod q has q² + O(q) points, and its degree-3 equation in 3 variables is below the CW threshold.
